minutes.headline: Finance Committee split 3-3 and failed to approve a higher recreation director hours request; approved reserve funds for town manager search 4-2.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a Parks request to raise the recreation director from 19 to 28 hours paid from the parks revolving fund, with debate over the revolving fund's legal status (53d vs 53e and a half). The motion tied and failed. It then backed a reserve fund transfer for a town manager search consultant, discussed the select board's communications policy, the draft financial policy, the Q3 FY24 financial report and trial balance, and committee updates.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at opening; none offered.
At closing, a committee member (not a resident) hoped the select board can work together more constructively.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee tied 3-3 on raising the recreation director's hours, paid from the parks revolving account, so the request failed.
The committee approved 4-2 the select board's request to move reserve funds for a town manager search consultant, instead of using ARPA money.
Before the tie vote, members debated the parks revolving fund's legal status and its balance under the state's revolving fund rules.
The committee reviewed the Q3 FY24 financial report, with investment income ahead of projection and charter tuition reimbursement lagging until the last quarter.
Members were asked to read the financial planning section of the draft financial policy before the August 5 meeting.

why_it_matters: The tie leaves the recreation director at the current hours, so any change to how parks staffing is paid for from fees now depends on a later vote.
The reserve fund transfer draws on money held for unforeseen needs, and the draft financial policy, if adopted, would set how the town plans and spends such funds.
